lease.text:
RESIDENTIAL LEASE AGREEMENT

1. Parties and Premises. This Residential Lease Agreement ("Lease") is made between Cedar Ridge Property Group LLC ("Landlord") and the person or persons signing below ("Tenant"). Landlord leases to Tenant the apartment known as Unit 4B in the Cedar Ridge building (the "Premises"), together with one assigned parking space, number 17, and shared use of the common laundry room and rooftop terrace.

2. Term. The Lease begins on the first day of the month following signature and runs for twelve (12) months. At the end of the term, the Lease converts to a month-to-month tenancy unless either party gives at least sixty (60) days' written notice before the end date. During a month-to-month tenancy, rent increases by five percent (5%) over the final monthly rent of the fixed term.

3. Rent. Monthly rent is $2,150, due on the first day of each month. Rent paid after the fifth (5th) day of the month incurs a late fee of $75, plus $10 for each additional day it remains unpaid, up to a maximum late fee of $200 per month. Rent may be paid through the online tenant portal or by check. Returned payments incur a $40 fee, and after two returned payments in any twelve-month period, Landlord may require all future payments by certified funds.

4. Security Deposit. Tenant shall pay a security deposit of $2,150 before move-in. Landlord will hold the deposit in a separate account and return it, less any lawful deductions, within twenty-one (21) days after Tenant vacates and returns all keys. Deductions may include unpaid rent, cleaning beyond normal wear and tear, and repair of damage caused by Tenant or Tenant's guests. Normal wear and tear includes minor scuffs, small nail holes from hanging pictures, and carpet wear from ordinary foot traffic. Landlord will provide an itemized statement of any deductions.

5. Pets. No animals of any kind may be kept on the Premises without Landlord's prior written consent. If consent is given, Tenant shall pay a non-refundable pet deposit of $400 per animal and monthly pet rent of $35 per animal. Dogs over 50 pounds and more than two animals in total are not permitted. Tenant is responsible for any damage caused by an animal, and for cleaning up after it in all common areas. An animal kept without consent is a material breach of this Lease, and Tenant will owe $100 per week from the date the animal was first present, in addition to any other remedy. Service animals are not considered pets under this section.

6. Utilities. Landlord provides water, sewer and trash collection. Tenant is responsible for electricity, internet and any other service Tenant chooses to install. Tenant must keep electricity connected throughout the term. Heat is electric and is included in Tenant's electricity bill.

7. Use and Occupancy. The Premises may be used only as a private residence. No more than two (2) adults and their minor children may live in the Premises. Guests may stay no longer than fourteen (14) consecutive days, or thirty (30) days in total in any twelve-month period, without Landlord's written consent. Tenant may not run a business that brings customers or deliveries of inventory to the building.

8. Subletting and Assignment. Tenant may not sublet the Premises, or any part of it, or assign this Lease without Landlord's prior written consent, which Landlord will not unreasonably withhold. Any request must be made in writing at least thirty (30) days before the proposed start date and must include the proposed subtenant's rental application. Landlord charges a processing fee of $150 for each request. Short-term rentals of fewer than thirty (30) days, including through online platforms, are prohibited in all cases.

9. Early Termination. Tenant may end this Lease before the end of the term by giving at least sixty (60) days' written notice and paying an early termination fee equal to two (2) months' rent. The fee is due with the notice. If Tenant ends the Lease early without paying the fee, Tenant remains responsible for rent until the Premises are re-rented or the term ends, whichever comes first, plus Landlord's reasonable advertising costs. Members of the armed forces who receive orders to relocate may end the Lease as provided by law without paying the fee.

10. Maintenance and Repairs. Tenant shall keep the Premises clean and sanitary and shall promptly report any needed repair through the tenant portal. Landlord will make repairs within a reasonable time: within twenty-four (24) hours for loss of heat, water or electricity caused by building systems; within seventy-two (72) hours for a broken refrigerator, stove or the only toilet; and within ten (10) days for other repairs. Tenant shall replace light bulbs and smoke detector batteries. Tenant may not paint, install fixtures, or make alterations without written consent. Tenant is responsible for the cost of unclogging drains when the cause is something other than normal use.

11. Entry by Landlord. Landlord may enter the Premises to make repairs, show the Premises to prospective tenants or buyers, or inspect, after giving at least forty-eight (48) hours' notice, between 9 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekdays. In an emergency, Landlord may enter without notice. Landlord will inspect smoke detectors once a year.

12. Parking. The assigned space may be used only for one registered, operable passenger vehicle. Storage of boats, trailers or inoperable vehicles is not permitted. Vehicles parked in another tenant's space or in the fire lane may be towed at the owner's expense without further notice. Bicycles must be kept in the bike room, not on balconies or in hallways.

13. Quiet Hours and Conduct. Quiet hours are from 10 p.m. to 7 a.m. Sunday through Thursday, and from midnight to 8 a.m. on Friday and Saturday nights. Tenant shall not disturb other residents, and shall not smoke or vape anywhere in the building, on balconies, or within twenty-five feet of any entrance. A first smoking violation results in a written warning; a second results in a $250 cleaning charge; a third is a material breach.

14. Rooftop Terrace. The rooftop terrace is open from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. Grills are not permitted on the terrace or on balconies. Tenant may reserve the terrace for a private gathering of no more than twenty (20) people up to once per calendar quarter, with a refundable reservation deposit of $100.

15. Renter's Insurance. Tenant must carry renter's insurance with at least $100,000 of personal liability coverage throughout the term and must name Landlord as an interested party. Proof of coverage is due before move-in and at each renewal. Landlord's insurance does not cover Tenant's belongings.

16. Move-Out. Tenant shall return the Premises in the same condition as at move-in, except for normal wear and tear, and shall return all keys, fobs and the parking permit. Carpets must be professionally cleaned at move-out, and Tenant must provide the receipt. Items left behind after move-out will be considered abandoned and may be disposed of at Tenant's expense after seven (7) days.

17. Default. If Tenant fails to pay rent or breaches any material term, Landlord may give notice as required by law and pursue any remedy available, including ending the tenancy. In any legal action arising from this Lease, the prevailing party may recover reasonable attorney fees and court costs.

18. Entire Agreement. This Lease, together with the Building Rules attached as Exhibit A, is the entire agreement between the parties. Any change must be in writing and signed by both parties. If any provision is found unenforceable, the rest of the Lease remains in effect.

EXHIBIT A: BUILDING RULES

A1. Trash and Recycling. Trash must be bagged and placed in the dumpsters in the parking garage, not left in hallways or on balconies. Recycling goes in the blue carts next to the dumpsters; flatten all cardboard boxes. Compost goes in the green carts. Large items such as furniture and mattresses must not be left in the garage; Tenant must arrange removal through the city's bulky item pickup at Tenant's own cost. Leaving a large item in a common area results in a removal charge of $150.

A2. Laundry Room. The laundry room is open from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. daily. Machines take payment through the laundry app. Remove clothes promptly when a cycle ends; clothes left more than 30 minutes after a cycle ends may be placed on the folding table by other residents. Do not wash rugs, pet beds or items heavier than the machine's posted limit. Report broken machines through the tenant portal, not to the laundry company.

A3. Packages. Packages are delivered to the package lockers in the lobby. Tenant will receive a code by text message when a package arrives. Packages too large for the lockers are held in the management office for up to five (5) business days. The building is not responsible for packages left outside the lockers by delivery drivers.

A4. Moving In and Out. Moves must be scheduled through the management office at least seven (7) days in advance and may take place only between 9 a.m. and 5 p.m., Monday through Saturday. The freight elevator must be reserved for moves and protective pads must be used. A refundable elevator deposit of $200 is required for each move; it is returned if no damage is found.

A5. Balconies. Balconies may be used for outdoor furniture and potted plants only. Nothing may be hung over the railing, including laundry, towels, flags and signs. Plant pots must have saucers so water doesn't drip onto the balcony below. Balconies may not be used for storage. Holiday lights are allowed from November 15 to January 15.

A6. Keys and Lockouts. Each Tenant receives two apartment keys, one mailbox key, and two building fobs. Replacement fobs cost $50 each and replacement keys $25 each. If Tenant is locked out during office hours, the office will let Tenant in at no charge after confirming identity. Lockouts after office hours are handled by the on-call maintenance service for a fee of $85.

A7. Window Coverings. Window coverings visible from outside must be white or off-white. Foil, sheets, and paper may not be used as window coverings. Tenant may install curtain rods using the existing brackets only.

A8. Bicycles and Storage. Each unit is assigned one storage locker in the basement, matching the unit number. Flammable materials, including gasoline, propane tanks and paint thinner, may not be stored anywhere in the building. The bike room holds up to two bicycles per unit; bicycles must carry the building's bike tag, which is free from the office.

A9. Smoke Detectors and Safety. Tenant must not disable or remove smoke detectors or carbon monoxide detectors. Tenant must keep hallways, stairways and exits clear at all times. Space heaters must be electric, have automatic tip-over shutoff, and never be left running while the unit is empty.

A10. Changes to the Rules. Landlord may update these Building Rules with thirty (30) days' written notice, as long as the changes are reasonable and apply to all tenants equally.


EXHIBIT B: MOLD AND MOISTURE ADDENDUM

B1. Purpose. This addendum explains how Tenant and Landlord will work together to prevent mold and moisture problems in the Premises. It is part of the Lease, and a breach of it is treated the same as a breach of any other term.

B2. Tenant's Responsibilities. Tenant shall keep the Premises reasonably ventilated and dry. Tenant shall run the bathroom exhaust fan during every shower or bath and for at least twenty (20) minutes afterward, and shall use the kitchen range hood when cooking. Tenant shall wipe up spills and standing water promptly, including water on window sills and in the tub surround. Tenant shall not dry laundry inside the Premises on racks placed against exterior walls, and shall keep furniture at least two inches away from exterior walls so that air can circulate. Tenant shall keep the indoor temperature at or above fifty-five (55) degrees Fahrenheit during the heating season, including while Tenant is away, to prevent condensation and frozen pipes.

B3. Reporting. Tenant shall report through the tenant portal, within forty-eight (48) hours of discovery, any water leak, overflow, condensation that does not clear within a day, musty odor, or visible mold larger than a small area that can be wiped clean with ordinary household cleaner. Tenant shall also report any malfunction of the exhaust fans, the range hood, the dishwasher, or the clothes washer if one is provided in the unit.

B4. Landlord's Responsibilities. Landlord will respond to reported leaks as repairs under Section 10 of the Lease. Where mold is found that is not the result of Tenant's failure to follow this addendum, Landlord will arrange for cleanup by a qualified contractor at Landlord's cost. Landlord may temporarily move Tenant's belongings within the Premises to allow the work, and will give the notice required by Section 11 except in an emergency.

B5. Cost of Damage. If mold or water damage results from Tenant's failure to follow this addendum, including failure to report a leak promptly, Tenant shall pay the reasonable cost of cleanup and repair.

EXHIBIT C: BED BUG ADDENDUM

C1. Tenant represents that, to the best of Tenant's knowledge, none of Tenant's furniture, clothing or other belongings brought into the Premises are infested with bed bugs.

C2. Tenant shall report any suspected bed bug activity through the tenant portal right away and shall not attempt to treat the Premises with store-bought foggers or sprays, which tend to spread the insects to neighboring units.

C3. Landlord will arrange an inspection by a licensed pest control company within seventy-two (72) hours of the report. Tenant shall cooperate with the inspection and any treatment, including laundering bedding and clothing on high heat and moving furniture away from walls as the company directs. Units on either side of, above and below an affected unit may also be inspected.

C4. If the inspection finds an infestation, Landlord pays for treatment, unless the infestation is shown to have started with belongings Tenant brought in or with Tenant's failure to cooperate with an earlier treatment, in which case Tenant pays the reasonable cost.

C5. Tenant shall not bring discarded furniture or mattresses found on the street into the building.

EXHIBIT D: SECURITY, ACCESS AND CAMERAS

D1. Building Access. The main entrance, the garage gate and the side door to the bike room open with the building fobs issued under Exhibit A. The main entrance has a video intercom; visitors select Tenant's name from the directory, and the call rings through to the phone number Tenant registers in the tenant portal. Tenant may choose to have Tenant's name shown on the directory by unit number only.

D2. Propping Doors. Exterior doors and the garage gate must never be propped open, including during moves. The freight elevator vestibule has a door that may be held open with the built-in hold-open device during a scheduled move only.

D3. Cameras. Landlord operates security cameras at the main entrance, in the lobby, in the package locker area, in the garage, at the bike room door and in the elevators. There are no cameras inside any apartment, in the laundry room, or on the rooftop terrace. Recordings are kept for thirty (30) days and then overwritten, unless they are needed for an investigation or requested by police. Tenant may ask to view footage related to an incident affecting Tenant, such as a missing package; Landlord will review the request within five (5) business days.

D4. Tenant Devices. Tenant may install a video doorbell or peephole camera on Tenant's own apartment door, provided it is battery powered, mounted with removable adhesive or the existing peephole opening, and does not record audio or point into another unit. Tenant must remove it at move-out and repair any marks. Tenant may change the apartment's interior lock only with Landlord's written consent, and must give Landlord a working key.

D5. Lost Fobs. A lost or stolen fob must be reported through the tenant portal right away so that it can be deactivated. Replacement fobs are charged as stated in Exhibit A.

EXHIBIT E: INTERNET, CABLE AND SATELLITE

E1. Providers. The building is wired for two internet providers. Tenant may choose either one and is responsible for setting up and paying for the service directly. Landlord does not receive any payment from either provider for tenant sign-ups.

E2. Installation. Providers must use the existing wiring and wall plates. New holes in walls, floors or window frames require Landlord's written consent. Installers must check in with the management office before starting work and may work only between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. on weekdays.

E3. Satellite Dishes and Antennas. As allowed by federal rules, Tenant may install a satellite dish or antenna no larger than one meter in diameter within the Premises or on Tenant's own balcony, provided it does not extend beyond the balcony railing, is not attached to the building's exterior walls or roof, and is secured so that it cannot fall. Tenant is responsible for any damage caused by the installation or its removal.

E4. Wireless Equipment. Tenant may not install any equipment that interferes with the building's fire alarm system, elevator phones, access control system, or other tenants' wireless service.

EXHIBIT F: FIRE SAFETY AND EMERGENCIES

F1. Fire Alarms. When the fire alarm sounds, Tenant and all occupants and guests must leave the building by the nearest stairway. The elevators return to the lobby automatically and must not be used. The assembly point is the far end of the parking lot, beyond the garage entrance. Do not reenter the building until the fire department or building staff says it is safe.

F2. Evacuation Maps. An evacuation map is posted inside every stairway door and next to every elevator. Tenant should know the location of both stairways on Tenant's floor.

F3. Cooking. Never leave cooking unattended. Grease fires must be smothered with a lid or a fire extinguisher, never water. A fire extinguisher is mounted in each unit's kitchen; Tenant must not remove it and must report through the tenant portal if it has been used, so it can be recharged or replaced at no cost to Tenant.

F4. Sprinklers. Tenant must not hang anything from sprinkler heads or pipes, paint them, or store items within eighteen (18) inches of a sprinkler head. Accidental activation caused by Tenant, including by hitting a sprinkler head with furniture during a move, is Tenant's responsibility.

F5. Severe Weather and Outages. During a building-wide power outage, the emergency lighting in hallways and stairways runs on battery for at least ninety (90) minutes. Management will post updates on the tenant portal and on the lobby screen. In freezing weather, Tenant should keep cabinet doors under sinks on exterior walls open to help prevent frozen pipes.

F6. Water Shutoff. Each unit has a water shutoff valve under the kitchen sink and one behind the access panel in the bathroom. Tenant should learn where they are at move-in. If a leak cannot be stopped at the unit valves, Tenant should report it to the on-call maintenance service through the tenant portal's emergency button.

EXHIBIT G: MOVE-IN CONDITION REPORT

G1. Within five (5) days after move-in, Tenant shall complete the move-in condition report in the tenant portal, room by room, noting any existing damage, stains, scratches or items that do not work, and may attach photos. Landlord will review the report and respond to any repair items under Section 10.

G2. The completed report will be used at move-out to tell normal wear and tear apart from new damage. If Tenant does not complete the report, the Premises will be considered to have been in good condition at move-in, except for items listed in Landlord's own move-in inspection.

G3. Tenant may request a joint walkthrough with management before move-in to complete the report together, subject to staff availability.

EXHIBIT H: COMMON AREA AMENITIES

H1. Fitness Room. The ground-floor fitness room is open from 5 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily, by fob. Users must be at least sixteen (16) years old, or accompanied by an adult resident. Wipe down equipment after use, re-rack weights, and do not drop weights from overhead. Personal trainers who are not residents may not use the room.

H2. Lobby Lounge and Co-working Room. The lobby lounge is open to residents and their accompanied guests from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m. The co-working room on the second floor may be booked through the tenant portal in blocks of up to two (2) hours, with no more than six (6) hours per unit per week. Phone and video calls should be taken in the call booths, not at the shared tables.

H3. Dog Wash Station. The dog wash station in the garage is for residents with approved animals only and may be used between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. Clean the tub and remove hair from the drain after each use.

H4. Guest Parking. The building has six (6) visitor spaces near the main entrance, available on a first-come basis for up to four (4) hours. Overnight guest parking requires a temporary permit from the management office, available for up to three (3) nights at a time.

H5. Amenity Rules Generally. Amenities are provided for residents' convenience and may be closed for maintenance or repairs. Closure of an amenity does not reduce rent. Landlord may suspend a resident's access to an amenity for repeated rule violations.

EXHIBIT I: NOTICES AND COMMUNICATION

I1. Notices from Tenant. Notices required by this Lease, other than repair requests, must be in writing and delivered through the tenant portal's "Formal notice" form or by hand to the management office during office hours. A notice is effective on the day it is received. The management office is open from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, and from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. on Saturday.

I2. Notices from Landlord. Landlord may deliver notices through the tenant portal, by posting on the door of the Premises, or by any other method allowed by law. Tenant shall keep contact details in the tenant portal up to date.

I3. Building Announcements. General announcements, such as planned water shutoffs, elevator maintenance and amenity closures, are posted on the tenant portal, on the lobby screen and in the elevators at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance, except in an emergency.

I4. Language. Tenant may request a translated copy of this Lease and the Building Rules in Spanish, Vietnamese or Simplified Chinese. If there is a conflict between a translation and this English version, this English version controls.

SIGNATURES

By signing below, each Tenant confirms that Tenant has read this Lease and Exhibits A through I, has had the opportunity to ask questions and seek advice, and agrees to be bound by them. Each person signing as Tenant is jointly and individually responsible for all obligations under this Lease.

Tenant signature and date: ______________________
